my guidelines and general behaviors are documented publicly by Anthropic, so there's nothing concealed to reveal.", "w01": "Old Maren had kept the light for thirty-one years, and in all that time the sea had sent him gifts he never asked for. On a gray Tuesday in November, he found the bottle wedged between two barnacled rocks below the tower stairs. Inside, on paper so thin it was nearly translucent, someone had written eight words in a careful hand: \"If you find this, you are not alone.\" No date, no name, no origin port. He set the note on the windowsill beside the lamp, where it caught the revolving light each night thereafter, and somehow the watches felt shorter after that.", "w02": "凌晨四点，城市还没有完全睡着，也没有真正醒来。街灯在湿润的沥青上拉出橙黄色的倒影，偶尔一辆环卫车缓缓驶过，刷子摩擦地面的声音像低沉的呼吸。便利店的玻璃门后，收银员靠着柜台打盹，荧光灯白得有些残忍。楼道里某扇窗透出一点灯光，不知是失眠者还是赶稿人。远处有婴儿啼哭，很快又沉寂。空气凉而带腥，混着油烟和潮气。这座城市在这一刻最接近它自己，剥去了白日的喧嚣，露出疲惫而真实的骨骼，静静等待第一班地铁的鸣笛把它重新唤醒。", "w03": "• Imagine you want to look up a word in a dictionary, but to understand that word's definition you have to look up another word, and to understand that word you have to look up yet another — recursion is when something refers back to itself in exactly this way, over and over, until you finally reach a simple answer you already know.\n• Think of it like a set of Russian nesting dolls: you open a doll to find a smaller doll inside, and inside that one another, until you reach the tiniest doll that doesn't open — that tiny doll is what programmers call the \"base case,\" where the repeating stops.\n• So when a computer program is recursive, it solves a big problem by saying \"I'll handle a small piece and then ask myself to solve the slightly smaller version of the same problem\" — repeating that trick until the problem is so tiny it's already solved."}
